items.title: Cone net:arc length must fit the base
items.student: Right cone:r3cm,verticalheight4cm,slant5cm. On blank paper construct a radius5cm sector of216°(equivalently remove144°from a full circle)and a separate radius3cm base disk;make/label the lateral net and disk with safe teacher-approved tools. Verify sector arc equals base circumference. Calculate lateral and total closed surface area;state which pieces a cone without base has. A labelled schematic is supplied,not physicalprintscale.

items.title: Square-pyramid net:four faces and a base
items.student: A right square pyramid has base side4cm and face slantheight3cm. Use supplied net:central4cmsquare and four outward isosceles triangles,eachbase4cm/perpendicularfaceheight3cm. Make/label a safe paper model or record accessible template adaptation. Compute lateral and closed total area;explain why faceheight is not verticalpyramidheight.

items.title: A rectangular base gives two face heights
items.student: Right rectangular pyramid:base8cm by6cm,verticalheight4cm. Derive face slantheight to each8cmedge and each6cmedge. Draw a net with centralrectangle,two8-base triangles and two6-base triangles;label corresponding heights. Compute lateral and closed area.

items.title: Hemisphere:which circular face is included?
items.student: Ideal hemisphere radius4cm. Compute curvedsurface only,then closed total including its circular cutface. Compare with a zero-thickness open dome/bowl model that counts only the curved outer surface. Explain why a real thick bowl’s inner/outer/rim areas require more dimensions and an explicit counted-surface statement.

items.title: Conical frustum:the end disks are separate
items.student: Right conical frustum has top radiusR5cm,bottomradiusr3cm and slantlengths4cm. Verify a feasible verticalheight,then compute curvedlateralareaπ(R+r)s. Compute totalclosedarea,open-topbucketarea withbottompresent,andopen-both-endsarea. Make a counted-face list before adding disks.

items.title: Square-pyramid frustum:four trapezoids
items.student: Right square-pyramid frustum has bottomsquare side6cm,topsquare side2cm,and each trapezoidalfaceperpendicularslantheight5cm. Draw a net partition into fourtrapezoidsplusendfaces. Compute lateral,closedtotal,open-topwithbottom,andopen-bothareas. Explain why a cone-frustum formula does not fit.

items.student: Use clean card/tape and teacher-approved blunt tools. Conefrustumscale model:topR2.5cm,bottomr1.5cm,slant2cm. Draw a half-annulus with outerradius5cm,innerradius3cm;join straight ends,then add separate circlesr1.5and2.5as removablebottom/top. Each learner contributes a named construction/measurement/check;compare open and closed counted surfaces.

items.title: Measure a safe spherical approximation
items.student: Teacher supplies a clean soft ball approximating a sphere and an approved empty plastic dome/hemisphere if available. Estimate diameter using two light parallel flat cards with a ruler gap;repeat along3directions and record actual readings/toolprecision. Compute an ideal sphere surfaceestimate;for dome declare curved-only or circularfaceincluded. Each learner makes a named measurement/record/check. Do not cut objects or force them between heavy books.

items.student: Fictional conical cover:r3m,slant5m,no base;find ideal outsidearea then add10%material allowance explicitly. Explain fit/seams/waste and why this does not certify engineering/safety.
